story: A wandering religious teacher was born in Lumbini to royal parents of the Shakya clan. He renounced his home life to live as a wandering ascetic. After a period of mendicancy, asceticism, and meditation, he attained nirvana at Bodh Gaya. He then wandered through the lower plain, teaching others and building a monastic order known as the sangha. He taught a Middle Way between sensual indulgence and severe asceticism, leading to freedom from ignorance, craving, rebirth, and suffering. His core teachings were summarized in the Four Noble Truths and the Noble Eightfold Path, a training of the mind that included ethical training, kindness toward others, and meditative practices such as sense restraint, mindfulness, and meditation proper. He also taught the concepts of the five aggregates and dependent origination, describing how all phenomena—both mental states and concrete things—come into being and cease to be depending on other phenomena, lacking an existence of their own. He frequently referred to himself by a special title meaning one who is beyond all coming and going. He was also known by many other epithets reflecting his perfected qualities, such as the Blessed One, the Well-Gone, the Knower of Worlds, and the Teacher of gods and humans. His followers compiled his teachings into two collections: one containing codes for monastic discipline, and another containing discourses attributed to him. Later generations composed additional texts, including systematic treatises, biographies, stories of his past lives, and further discourses. Tradition holds that he died in Kushinagar and reached final release from conditioned existence.
